title: Phawar of Hearth Dining Etiquette (Akor Bam Akor Dih)
cultural_context: Rhyming rules of eating and drinking at table and hearth, forbidding gluttony, greed, and bad manners, from Radhon Singh Berry's 'Ka Jingsneng Tymmen'.

khasi: Haba phi bam ja phi dih um,
Wat leh lalot, wat khwan kpoh shuh;
Khein kor ia uba shong lang ha dpei,
Buh akor ia ka ja bad ka doh;
Ka rukom bam ka pynpaw bha,
Lada phi san ha ka akor;
Uba bam da ka burom briew
U pynkmen ia la ka kmie bad u kpa.
english: Whenever you partake of rice and drink of water,
Be not gluttonous, show no greedy appetite;
Honor those who sit alongside you at the hearth,
Respect the sustenance of rice and meat;
The manner of one's dining clearly reveals
Whether you were reared in noble discipline;
He who eats with dignity and self-restraint
Brings pride and joy unto his mother and father.

khasi: Wat bam dait-kdait, wat pashat ja,
Wat kren da ka ktien ba khlem akor;
U Blei Uba Khraw U theh ia ka ja,
To bam da ka jingai-nguh ba shai,
Ha ryngkat ka dohnud ba kmen;
Ba ka jingim jong phi kan roi
Ha ka koit ka khiah ba neh.
english: Eat not noisily, scatter no grains of rice,
Utter no coarse words during the meal;
Almighty God has provided our daily bread,
As a precious blessing of His grace;
Accompanied by a joyful and peaceful spirit;
So that your life may flourish and thrive
In lasting health, vitality, and strength.
